This directive distribution, imperatives at the frame's two ends bracketing a directive-free middle, is what fixes the unit's own bounds rather than any split within it.

Three byte-grounded binders carry across the zone's internal seams. The negated-knowledge refrain interlocks the opening, middle and close: לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) collates at accent-stripped tier against כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte), and אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) collates at skeleton tier against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte); each attested form is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the know-negation, web:Eccl.11.2 and web:Eccl.11.5; sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the negated-existential form, web:Eccl.11.5 and web:Eccl.11.6), with all four sites falling inside this unit. The zone's directive forms cluster at its two ends: שַׁלַּ֥ח (oshb:Eccl.11.1, tier: byte), "send", opens the counsel, matching “Cast your bread on the waters” (web:Eccl.11.1); תֶּן (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte), "give", continues it, matching “Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight” (web:Eccl.11.2); and the unit closes with זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "sow", paired with the negative אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "do not let...rest", matching “In the morning sow your seed...in the evening don't withhold your hand” (web:Eccl.11.6). The three middle verses carry no second-person directive at all: v.3 opens a conditional protasis, אִם...עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte); v.4 is a participial clause with a negated prefix-conjugation, שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte); and v.5 is a comparative declarative. This directive distribution, imperatives at the frame's two ends bracketing a directive-free middle, is what fixes the unit's own bounds rather than any split within it.

Three byte-grounded binders carry across the zone's internal seams. The negated-knowledge refrain interlocks the opening, middle and close: לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) collates at accent-stripped tier against כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte), and אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) collates at skeleton tier against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte); each attested form is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the know-negation, web:Eccl.11.2 and web:Eccl.11.5; sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the negated-existential form, web:Eccl.11.5 and web:Eccl.11.6), with all four sites falling inside this unit. The seam at 11:2/11:3 itself carries a repeated phrase, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte), word-bound at skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and 11:2/11:3 the only adjacent pair among them). A third binder ties the declarative middle to the closing imperative: the same triliteral sowing root (ז-ר-ע) stands in יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte) and in זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), different inflected forms of the one root, not a word-bound identity, but book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside it). No byte warrant separates any internal seam that these three binders do not themselves cross.

Both outer bounds hold clean on content rather than chapter numbering: the back seam shares with the preceding verse only a causal particle, a function word, and that verse closes its own sentence zone (web:Eccl.10.20); the forward seam shares with the following verse only the object marker, and that verse opens the light-frame that begins the aging-allegory zone (web:Eccl.11.7).

neighbour_prev_post_repair.boundary_rationale: A single admonition-sentence closes the chapter. Its actual opening words are גַּ֣ם בְּמַדָּֽעֲךָ֗ (oshb:Eccl.10.20, tier: byte) — "even in your thought" — with the curse clauses following, spliced as מֶ֚לֶךְ אַל תְּקַלֵּ֔ל (oshb:Eccl.10.20, tier: byte) — "the king, do not curse" — matching “Don’t curse the king” (web:Eccl.10.20). Near its close stands an inline ketiv/qere pair, הכנפים כְּנָפַ֖יִם (oshb:Eccl.10.20, ketiv/qere; tier: byte), on the word for "wings," matching “that which has wings may tell the matter” (web:Eccl.10.20). The verse carries a doubled negated prefix-conjugation (jussive-pattern) form used for negative commands, not a true imperative ("do not curse the king...do not curse the rich"); it is one grammatical sentence and is held as a single_saying under the sentence-zone default, closing the chapter.
neighbour_prev_post_repair.strongest_rejected_alternative: Classifying this verse as an admonition_unit rather than single_saying is rejected because the whole warning is confined to one grammatical sentence rather than a multi-verse counsel block.

neighbour_next_post_repair.boundary_rationale: The bridge opens in third-person reflection, “Truly the light is sweet” (web:Eccl.11.7), turning at v.8 to a conditional: כִּ֣י אִם שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — "if a man lives many years" — followed by its own apodosis, בְּכֻלָּ֣ם יִשְׂמָ֑ח (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — “let him rejoice in them all” (web:Eccl.11.8), and its own remember-clause, וְיִזְכֹּר֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — "and let him remember" — matching “let him remember the days of darkness” (web:Eccl.11.8). At v.9 the register shifts to direct second-person vocative address, spliced as שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר (oshb:Eccl.11.9, tier: byte) — "rejoice, young man" — matching “Rejoice, young man, in your youth” (web:Eccl.11.9). Both halves are held as one row because the rejoice root recurs at v.8 and v.9 (though the remember root stands at 1 of 4 verses in the span, v.8, not repeated at v.9-10), continuing without a discourse-frame break; the 3rd-to-2nd-person shift at v.8/9 is disclosed as a live alternative seam. An unbroken 2ms-imperative chain — שְׂמַ֧ח (oshb:Eccl.11.9) here, וְהָסֵ֥ר (oshb:Eccl.11.10) in the verse that follows, and וּזְכֹר֙ (oshb:Eccl.12.1) in the unit after that — together with the near-identical youth-phrase catchword (בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Eccl.11.9) against בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Eccl.12.1), sweep: 2 verses) both cross this unit's own closing seam into the poem that follows; the row still closes at v.10 because the register there completes the youth-address begun at v.9, while the imperative chain's continuation into the poem is disclosed as cross-seam texture rather than adopted as a boundary shift. The unit closes on “youth and the dawn of life are vanity” (web:Eccl.11.10), immediately before the aging-allegory poem's own imperative opens.
